rationale: The complete canonical question and preserved ORIGINAL were read; I checked both retained manuscript model paragraphs and Colbrook's explicit zero-variable boundary. Initial numerical registers are only the real coordinates. Context-indexed finite Program constructors exactly allow stored output, exact negation, independently rounded binary addition/subtraction/multiplication and exact three-way comparison. Persistent appending is an explicit faithful encoding of finite register reuse; no literal, hidden zero default, coefficient scaling or Boolean-to-real conversion is available.

The static all-branch rounded-node count and contiguous error-vector slicing give each syntactic operation one error coordinate while retaining prior rounded values at every reuse. Comparisons inspect actual current values and preserve equality and error-dependent branch changes. Unselected error coordinates are universally quantified and ignored. Every evaluator is finite without an adaptive loop, semantic function oracle or repeated-expression recomputation.

Exact correctness follows the actual zero-error path. The same finite program precedes every requested relative accuracy eta; only a uniform positive u follows eta, before every real input and error vector. The full unbounded real domain, polynomial zeros, non-strict error bounds and error-box endpoints remain. No genericity, probabilistic rounding, absolute error floor or branch-stability restriction was introduced.

The finite integer coefficient/exponent-list encoding includes dimension, length, all signed coefficients and every exponent. Duplicates, zero terms and arbitrary order are permitted with exact summation, so collected constant cancellation is respected. ValidInput only imposes p(0)=0. No symbolic coefficient becomes a numerical evaluator input. With zero variables the exact constant-free/output-register convention admits no Program 0; this degenerate no-instance is disclosed and matches the retained manuscript, while positive dimensions permit the zero polynomial via a rounded self-subtraction.

Target fixes one genuine finite ordinary binary machine before every valid polynomial and requires actual terminal one-bit output. Its finite time witness follows each input, with no polynomial bound. Existence of a rounded tree is the exact decidand; neither the signed-gap criterion nor a semantic decision oracle replaces it. Uniform syntax/evaluator semantics and actual source correspondence must be inspected again at final review. No numerical enumeration is needed to state the problem.

The complete canonical original and specification were read. The question is existence of one always-halting ordinary Turing decider for accurate finite-tree existence, not accuracy of a supplied tree, a complexity bound, or an assumed signed-gap criterion. The proposed Target retains that complete existential question and keeps construction of a successful evaluator as separate stronger proof material.

PolynomialInput contains every integer coefficient occurrence and all natural exponents in a finite list of fixed dimension. Exact sum/product semantics collect duplicates through addition, allow zero coefficients and noncanonical list order, and use the ordinary zero-power convention. ValidInput checks precisely p(0)=0, including cancellation of listed constant monomials. No homogeneity or normalized-support promise appears.

The input grammar writes framed dimension, term count, each signed integer coefficient and every coordinate exponent in fixed order. It describes a concrete finite encoding using the already-reviewed binary primitives. Since no runtime bound is prescribed, choosing a computably interconvertible sparse coefficient list does not impose a hidden polynomial translation requirement. These symbolic integers are Turing input, never free numerical constants for the rounded evaluator.

Program r is finite inductive control-flow syntax whose only constructors return an available register, append exact negation, append a rounded binary add/subtract/multiply result, or branch on exact comparison of available values. Register indices are bounded by the current r, the initial vector is exactly x, and no implicit zero/one/default-output register is introduced.

Appending versions and retaining every old register is a faithful representation of finite storage and copying: later references reuse the same numerical value and its existing error dependence. Overwriting finite named registers can be represented by renaming subsequent references to appended versions. Finite bounded control flow can be unfolded into this tree; conversely every constructor is an allowed canonical operation. No arbitrary real function or unbounded loop replaces syntax.

Comparisons act on actual current real values and select less/equal/greater continuations with the same unchanged registers. Their outcomes can depend on previous errors and do not produce numeric Boolean constants. Equality branches and comparisons involving raw, negated and rounded values are retained. Exact negation consumes no rounding coordinate.

The static rounded-node count is zero at returns, unchanged by negation, incremented at each rounded node and summed over every comparison subtree. The explicit structural slices preserve preorder offsets for less/equal/greater, including skipped branches. A coordinate belongs to a distinct syntactic operation, while repeated reads of a stored result neither recompute nor allocate errors. Finite-vector evaluation therefore has exactly the canonical N(P) error domain.

Every allowed error vector is universally quantified with independent arbitrary coordinate choices, not a random law, deterministic operand-dependent rounding rule or chosen execution oracle. The specification permits a stream implementation only with the same finite public domain and a structurally checked no-outside-read property, so that simplification cannot enlarge the model.

Accuracy separately requires actual zero-error execution to equal the polynomial at every input. One fixed P precedes every eta in (0,1); then u in (0,1) precedes every real x and every error vector in the full closed box. Thus u cannot depend on x, ties, branch or error choice, and zeros force exact output for every allowed error. No absolute-error floor, bounded domain or generic-input restriction changes the target.

The natural-dimension edge case is explicitly supported by the retained Colbrook model-boundary paragraph: with zero inputs no register-valued output tree can be formed, so the valid zero-variable zero polynomial is a no-instance. With positive dimension a rounded x0-x0 tree computes zero for every error. The specification does not silently add an input variable or a constant-zero output constructor.

Target uses the actual previously reviewed finite binary machine and exact one-bit terminal output. Its machine is chosen before every valid polynomial input, but its finite time witness T follows that input and is unconstrained by a PolynomialBound. Every valid encoding must halt correctly; malformed words and nonzero-constant inputs are outside the stated domain. No quantifier-elimination, real comparison or tree-existence oracle is added to the binary machine.

The Stepaniants precise-model section and halting Corollary 7.1, plus Colbrook Section 1 and model-boundary paragraphs, were inspected directly. They require the same exact inputs, stored-value reuse, available-value outputs, error-dependent comparisons, all-branch node numbering, whole-real-space accuracy and absence of additional primitives. The specification correctly leaves collected-coefficient signed-gap tests and evaluator construction as future proof work, not target assumptions.

The primary Demmel-Dumitriu-Holtz model sections independently confirm bounded finite evaluation, exact negation/comparisons, separately selectable errors and stored-result reuse. That source also discusses broader primitive sets; the canonical restricted primitive set, rather than those broader variants, controls this review. [Primary model, Sections 2.1-2.7](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0508350v2#S2).

The proposed future kernel controls address meaningful operational distinctions: reuse versus recomputation, error-dependent equality, static offsets past unused branches, zero-error correctness, exact negation and the absent Program 0. No numerical sampling or criterion theorem is required simply to state the complete question, but the eventual implementation must have concrete structural semantics and independently reviewed full helper closure.

Comparison branches use fixed offsets zero, less-count and less-plus-equal-count, with explicit checked bounds. The roundedCount includes every branch. Actual current real values determine the comparison, including ties and error-dependent paths. Stored reuse retains the same earlier error factor; independent recomputation receives another coordinate.

ValidInput tests the collected p(0), allowing constant cancellation. Encoding contains dimension, list length and all coefficient/exponent fields in fixed order using unchanged reviewed finite binary primitives. Coefficients do not become real evaluator registers.

Accurate keeps one finite program before all eta, then one uniform positive u before all real inputs and independent error vectors. Exact zero-error correctness follows the actual path. The full relative inequality includes polynomial zeros with no exceptional set, absolute floor or probabilistic interpretation. Program0 is impossible by the actual constructor indices, matching the disclosed source boundary; positive-dimensional self-subtraction computes the zero polynomial under every error.

Target fixes one genuine ordinary finite binary decision machine before every valid coefficient-list input and requires its exact Boolean answer in a finite input-dependent time. It imposes no polynomial bound and assumes no signed-gap, real-quantifier-elimination or tree-existence oracle. The full imported finite machine and encoding are unchanged. Program r is genuine finite inductive syntax with only register return, exact negation, rounded add/subtract/multiply and three-way comparison. Every operand and output is Fin r. No constant register, arbitrary real function, oracle, loop, division, exact sum/product or test-to-number instruction appears. The next arithmetic state has one appended register; previous indices are unchanged.

Program.evaluate is structural recursion over the actual finite tree. Fin.snoc preserves every old register and appends precisely the real arithmetic result times (1+delta), or exact negative. The pinned snoc definition and its castSucc/last identities were inspected. Stored result reuse preserves earlier error dependence; another rounded instruction, even with equal operands, uses a distinct coordinate.

roundedCount includes all rounded nodes across all branches. Each rounded node takes coordinate zero and supplies its successor tail. Comparison branches receive exactly disjoint blocks beginning at zero, less.count and less.count+equal.count. errorSlice constructs Fin indices with actual in-range proofs; no default zero error or inaccessible coordinate exists. Branch selection uses current rounded register values with exact less/equal/greater trichotomy.

Term and PolynomialInput contain actual integer coefficients, natural exponent vectors and a finite list. PolynomialValue sums every occurrence, including duplicate monomials and zero coefficients, using genuine natural powers and complete finite products. ValidInput is the collected p(0)=0 condition, preserving cancelled constant terms. Coefficients enter the symbolic encoding only, never the initial numerical registers.

encodePolynomial contains natural dimension and list length, then each signed coefficient and every exponent in increasing coordinate order. Its reused BinaryEncoding primitives use bit-length framing and canonical signed magnitudes. No coefficient, sign, exponent or count is omitted; the grammar has no output-dependent semantics. General inversion proofs remain future proof work, not an encoding oracle.

Accurate requires exact zero-error evaluation on every real input and then forall eta in (0,1), exists one u in (0,1), forall all real x and all independently bounded finite errors, the stated weak relative inequality. The same program is chosen before eta, and u is uniform over x/errors. Polynomial zeros force exact output zero. There is no absolute floor, probability law, generic-input guard or stable-branch assumption.

AccuratelyEvaluable quantifies actual finite Program syntax, not a supplied predicate or signed-gap criterion. At n=0 the no_program_zero proof inspects every constructor and its impossible Fin 0 index. The valid zero-variable polynomial is therefore a no-instance under the explicitly approved convention. For n=1, the control zero_tree_accurate proves exact subtraction zero for every error, including the full precision quantifier.

Target chooses a single ordinary FiniteMachine before every valid PolynomialInput, then a Boolean and a natural finite halting-time witness. The current shared finite alphabet/control table, actual TM0 trace, terminality and exact one-bit DecidesWithin semantics were inspected. No uniform polynomial time bound, real-equality oracle or gain/evaluator output is demanded. Behavior outside valid coefficient inputs remains unconstrained as specified.

All semantic controls were read. They check the square of a reused rounded sum, separate errors for recomputation, exact negation, equality and rounding-dependent comparison paths, branch-size counts, the greater/equal static error offsets, unused-branch independence, complete coefficient/exponent grammar, exact zero-polynomial accuracy and collected constant cancellation. Kernel trust is asserted for these meaningful symbolic checks; none proves the decidability target.

The final live/frozen modules import the same nominal Program/PolynomialInput and recursive evaluator definitions from RoundedTree.
